title: I Took the Embroidery-Machine Reservation to the Mentor Who Hijacked the Hoop

parts.text: I loaded my file at 6:31 p.m. and mentor Lia had already hooped a club banner on my reserved machine. The calendar said: NINETY MINUTES. UNLOAD ON THE BEEP. I was thirty, stitcher, holding a calendar invite. Lia did not unload. "Banners are the shop." I photographed the invite, the hoop, and the beep history. Then I logged a hijack. At 6:39 the makerspace desk asked why Lia's banner was on my ninety. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The makerspace desk can see Lia's banner hoop on my ninety-minute invite.

social.video_title: She hooped a banner on my reserved machine — Part 1/2
social.description: Embroidery, a calendar invite, and a mentor's banner. I logged the hijack. Would you have waited for the beep?

parts.text: Lia called it a deadline until the desk asked for the log. I printed the hijack, the photo, and the invite. The hoop came off. Lia reserved banner time and told stitchers deadlines were always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when a hoop exists. Reservation now has a second line: BANNERS BOOK TOO. I keep my ninety. Lia queues. The machine finally stitches a file, not a title. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.

social.description: Hijack log, unloaded hoop, and a second line. Was a deadline ever my invite?
